A1.justification: Both PDFs describe SGEquiDiff, with matching core methods, theorems, datasets, and figures. Their complete text, tables, equations, and appendices are readable and support comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original MP20 and MPTS52 generation experiments, temperature and lattice-sampler ablations, and DFT stability and displacement results.

after.justification: V2 retains original generation and DFT results and reports additional component ablations and composition-conditioned crystal structure prediction experiments.

M1.justification: V2 adds a CSP procedure combining the existing pretrained +LDiff variant with CSPML template selection and element substitution. Section 4.1 also describes p(G) as empirical training frequencies instead of cross-entropy-trained logits. The main architecture and diffusion pipeline remain.

E1.justification: MP20 and MPTS52 generation coverage is retained. V2 adds composition-conditioned crystal structure prediction on MP20, requiring recovery of test structures from supplied elemental compositions, a distinct task from unconditional generation.

E2.justification: The retained MPTS52 comparison expands from SymmCD's two externally reported validity scores to evaluations including DiffCSP, DiffCSP++, and fuller SymmCD results (Table 2). The MP20 generation comparator set remains unchanged. V2 also supplies a four-baseline CSP comparison in Table 3.

E3.justification: Sections 5 and A.5 change the stated stability reference from Materials Project v2024.11.14 to v2022.8.23, although v2 retains inconsistent MP-2024 column labels. V2 adds template novelty evaluation and a CSP protocol using one sample per composition, match rate, normalized RMSE, and distinct matching tolerances. New network ablations control parameter count; the temperature sweep drops T=1.1.

E4.justification: Beyond the existing lattice-sampler and temperature ablations, v2 tests replacement of symmetry features with SymmCD features and replacement of the denoising network with CSPNet (Table 5). The retained LDiff analysis gains a quantitative positive-determinant check, with 98.95% for +LDiff versus 100% for SGEquiDiff (Table 6).

E5.justification: V2 first reports standard deviations over three training runs for SGEquiDiff generation metrics and ablations (Tables 1, 2, 5, and 6). V1 provided no corresponding run-count or variability reporting, although its DFT displacement table already included standard deviations. This establishes expanded reporting, not an increase from a known earlier run count; S.U.N. uncertainty remains unquantified.

E6.justification: Tables 1–2 replace many SGEquiDiff results and add template novelty and baseline entries. S.U.N. values change from 12.47% to 25.80% for SGEquiDiff and 7.77% to 22.44% for MatterGen, under the revised stated stability reference. New CSP results include 69.42% match rate and 0.0416 RMSE for SGEquiDiff+LDiff+CSPML. Appendix ablation results are added; DFT displacement statistics and crystal examples are retained.

T1.justification: V2 corrects missing logarithms in the score-matching loss and score-normalization expressions in Section 4.4 and Appendix A.2, changing the written gradient of p to the gradient of log p. The two theorems and substantive proof arguments remain; edits to Theorem 1's proof mainly rename variables.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution list, and conclusion retain the same central claims: space-group-invariant likelihoods, tangent-space-preserving equivariant flows, autoregressive lattice generation, and state-of-the-art stable, unique, novel generation. Added experiments support these claims without redefining them.

C2.justification: V2 adds substantive CSP qualifications concerning unknown atom counts, multiple structures per composition, and sparse discovery regimes. It explains negative LDiff lattice determinants as symmetry violations for chiral space groups, replacing v1's NaN-lattice discussion. It also expands the rationale for factorized generation and interpretations of component ablations.

D1.justification: V2 adds a code repository link and substantially expands feature-construction documentation, including collision handling and the Fourier-feature recipe (A.5.1). It newly specifies masking behavior, absence of positional encoding, DFT energy corrections, baseline sizes, and ablation controls. These disclosures do not establish previously undocumented implementation changes. Core hardware, training times, splits, and hyperparameter listings are retained.

R1.justification: V2 adds three references: two Jain et al. works supporting DFT energy corrections and Satorras et al. on E(n)-equivariant networks. It expands comparisons with existing symmetry features and networks, while the Related Work section and central novelty positioning remain substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: V2 makes localized explanatory rewrites, expands method clarifications, separates ablation discussion, and moves feature descriptions into an expanded appendix subsection. It adds acknowledgments and revises affiliations and conference information. The overall narrative and section sequence remain recognizable rather than extensively rewritten.

P2.justification: Tables 1–2 gain template columns, expanded captions, and revised row structures. V2 adds CSP Table 3 and component-ablation Table 5, and separates the existing LDiff comparison into Table 6 with an additional determinant column. Figures 1–5 and the displacement table are retained apart from placement, numbering, and minor labels.

improvement.justification: V2 substantially strengthens empirical support: v1's sparse MPTS52 comparison and lack of training-run uncertainty are addressed through broader comparisons, three-run variability reporting, and controlled component ablations. CSP evaluation and expanded code-access and implementation documentation improve assessment and reproducibility. These gains outweigh limited reporting inconsistencies, including stale MP-2024 headers and a CSPNet composition-validity claim unsupported by a Table 5 value. The higher S.U.N. scores themselves do not establish improvement because the stated stability reference changes and DFT uncertainty remains unresolved.
